starterQuestions.q: What is the difference between interspecific and intraspecific variation?
starterQuestions.a: Interspecific is variation between distinct species; intraspecific is variation among individuals of the same species.

starterQuestions.q: What three primary biological processes generate genetic diversity in sexually reproducing organisms?
starterQuestions.a: Meiosis (crossing over and independent assortment), random fertilisation of gametes, and DNA mutations.

starterQuestions.q: Define phenotypic variance in the quantitative equation Vp = Vg + Ve.
starterQuestions.a: Total observable phenotypic variance (Vp) equals genetic variance (Vg) plus environmental variance (Ve).

starterQuestions.q: Why must ABO blood group data be plotted on a bar chart rather than a histogram?
starterQuestions.a: ABO blood groups are discrete, discontinuous qualitative categories, so bars must have distinct spaces between them.

starterQuestions.q: When is a histogram used instead of a bar chart for biological data?
starterQuestions.a: For continuous quantitative variables grouped into contiguous class intervals/bins (with no spaces between bars).

starterQuestions.q: What does the standard deviation measure in a biometric dataset?
starterQuestions.a: The spread or dispersion of individual continuous phenotypic values around the calculated arithmetic mean.

courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology - Unit F172: Genetics
focus: Phenotypic Variation, Origins of Genetic Diversity & Biometric Analysis
deliverable: Construct biometric plots (bar charts for discontinuous vs histograms for continuous traits), calculate and interpret standard deviation, and analyze blood-group genetics alongside the variance equation Vp = Vg + Ve.

objectives.knowledge: Explain how phenotypic variation reflects genetic, environmental, and combined influences, distinguishing interspecific vs intraspecific and continuous vs discontinuous variation.
objectives.application: Outline how genetic diversity arises via meiosis, random fertilisation, and mutation, applying these principles to ABO blood-group genetics.
objectives.evaluation: Select and construct appropriate graphical representations (bar charts vs histograms) and evaluate datasets using mean and standard deviation.

terminology.def: Interspecific: phenotypic variation between different species. Intraspecific: phenotypic variation between individuals of the same species.
A quantitative phenotypic spectrum controlled polygenically with environmental modifiers, plotted as a histogram.
Discrete, non-overlapping phenotypic categories determined by single-gene loci (e.g. ABO blood group), plotted as a bar chart.
A statistical metric quantifying the spread of continuous phenotypic measurements around the arithmetic mean: s = sqrt(sum(x - mean)^2 / (n - 1)).
Monogenic codominant/recessive single-locus system (alleles IA, IB, IO) showing strictly discontinuous genetic inheritance.

theoryPoints: Variation Framework: Phenotypic variation (Vp = Vg + Ve) includes interspecific differences (between species) and intraspecific differences (within species).
Origins of Diversity: Meiosis (crossing over in Prophase I, independent assortment in Metaphase I), random fertilisation of gametes, and spontaneous mutations.
Graph Selection: Discontinuous traits (ABO blood groups) require separated bar charts; continuous traits (height, blood pressure) require contiguous histograms.
Standard Deviation: In a standard normal biometric distribution, 68.2% of individuals lie within 1 standard deviation (mean +/- 1 SD), and 95.4% lie within 2 standard deviations.

workedExample.title: Biometric & Blood-Group Statistical Analysis
workedExample.subtitle: Comparing discontinuous ABO phenotypes and continuous biometric parameters

steps.label: Step 1: Categorising the Trait
steps.detail: ABO blood group is discontinuous (categories A, B, AB, O; monogenic IA, IB, IO; Ve = 0). Height or FEV1 is continuous (polygenic + environmental; Vp = Vg + Ve).

steps.label: Step 2: Graphical Selection
steps.detail: Plot ABO frequencies on a bar chart with spaces between categories. Plot height or blood pressure on a histogram with contiguous class intervals (e.g. 150-154 cm, 155-159 cm).

steps.label: Step 3: Calculating Central Tendency & Spread
steps.detail: For continuous data, calculate the arithmetic mean (e.g. 170 cm) and standard deviation s = 8 cm (variance s^2 = 64 cm^2).

steps.label: Step 4: Statistical Interpretation
steps.detail: Approximately 68% of the cohort falls between 162 cm and 178 cm (mean +/- 1 SD), and 95% falls between 154 cm and 186 cm (mean +/- 2 SD).

hingeQuestions.question: Which biological mechanism generates new, novel alleles rather than simply reshuffling existing parental alleles?
hingeQuestions.explanation: Mutations are the only source of novel alleles. Meiosis (crossing over and independent assortment) and random fertilisation reshuffle existing alleles into new combinations.

hingeQuestions.question: A student records the blood groups (A, B, AB, O) of 200 students. How should this data be displayed graphically?
options: A line graph connecting the data points
A bar chart with spaces between distinct qualitative categories
A histogram with contiguous bins and no spaces
A scatter plot with a line of best fit
hingeQuestions.explanation: ABO blood group is discontinuous qualitative data with distinct discrete categories, which must be displayed as a bar chart with spaces between bars.

hingeQuestions.question: In a biometric cohort of adult standing height (mean = 175 cm, standard deviation = 10 cm), what percentage of individuals is expected between 165 cm and 185 cm in a normal distribution?
hingeQuestions.explanation: In a normal distribution, approximately 68.2% of the population lies within 1 standard deviation of the mean (175 +/- 10 cm).

examQuestion.question: Distinguish between continuous and discontinuous variation in humans, using blood groups and height as examples. In your answer, explain how genetic diversity arises during sexual reproduction and describe how standard deviation and appropriate graphical presentations (bar charts vs histograms) are used to analyze biometric datasets. [6 marks]
guidance: Continuous vs Discontinuous Distinctions: Discontinuous variation shows discrete categories with no intermediates (monogenic, e.g. ABO blood groups; Ve=0); continuous variation forms a smooth numerical continuum (polygenic, e.g. height, modulated by Vp = Vg + Ve) [2 marks].

Origins of Genetic Diversity: Explain that meiosis (crossing over in Prophase I, independent assortment in Metaphase I) and random fertilisation reshuffle alleles, while mutations create novel alleles [2 marks].

Graphical and Statistical Analysis: Discontinuous data is plotted on bar charts with spaces between bars; continuous data is grouped into class intervals and plotted on histograms. Standard deviation quantifies spread around the mean (68% within 1 SD in normal distribution) [2 marks].

plenary: Phenotypic variation reflects genetic, environmental, and combined influences, manifesting as interspecific and intraspecific diversity.
Genetic diversity is generated through meiosis, random fertilisation, and mutations.
Master graphical selection (bar charts for discontinuous vs histograms for continuous) and standard deviation analysis.
Next Lesson: DNA structure, telomeres & replication — the molecular machinery of genetic inheritance.
